lore_anchors.definition: A secret fire-thunder of the demonic sect Qing Yang Gate, known for immense power rivaling a Nascent Soul cultivator's Primordial Yang Fire; its possession marks a cultivator as a close disciple of the Three Yang Old Devil.
An irregular powerhouse of the Demonic Path whose actions are unpredictable; his reputation alone is enough to make even Man Brutal Beard hesitate to pursue a grudge.
The floating jade palace in the sky, a central dungeon of this arc where sects compete for the legendary Void Heaven Cauldron.
A classic Chinese idiom describing a chain of predation where a hunter is about to be hunted by a hidden, greater power; the structural principle of this chapter.
A cultivator who has condensed a Golden Core; in the Mortal Stream, they are still ants before Nascent Soul cultivators, as demonstrated by the casual killing in this chapter.
A private communication method using spiritual sense, undetectable by others unless the listener has a far higher cultivation level.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Man Brutal Beard kill the Core Formation cultivator but spare Yuan Yao?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He killed the man casually, but Yuan Yao escaped using Green Fire Thunder, a secret technique that marked her as the Three Yang Old Devil's close disciple—a figure even Man Brutal Beard is wary of.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Wu Chou suddenly being so friendly to Han Li?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Extreme Yin Patriarch likely told Wu Chou to keep Han Li close, implying that Han Li's usefulness will end once the treasure is secured.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who are the Star Palace elders and why are they hiding?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are the true 'orioles' of this chapter; Star Palace cracked the Void Heaven Palace's teleportation restrictions a thousand years ago, allowing them to enter secretly and ambush the exhausted treasure-seekers.
